subject: Post-call: FinCrest latency targets & warm-pool / queueing expectations
messages:
From: Sophie Clarke <sophie.clarke@fincrest.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-22T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + SLO targets from today

Thanks for the call earlier, Camila — appreciate the walkthrough. Short recap from our side and the constraints we need to validate during technical onboarding:

- Workload: user-facing streaming transcription + short completion steps (avg response ~300 tokens).
- Target latency: p95 end-to-end generation (first-byte visible for streaming) <= 250 ms for 256-token segments; p95 for full-response latency <= 450 ms on typical requests.
- Concurrency/throughput: expected steady-state concurrency ~45-60 live sessions, spike concurrency up to ~120 for short bursts (3-5 minutes). Peak qps estimate: 180–220 qps during marketing events.
- Streaming constraints: chunk latency must be <100 ms for perception of realtime (we send partial tokens every 50-150 tokens).
- Scale-up expectation: we need ramp to degradable state within 60s for warm pool-backed capacity, and good degraded behavior if cold start occurs (graceful queueing, 503s only as last resort).
- Acceptance: if Redwood can demonstrably meet p95 targets and show autoscale from warm pool within ~5–12s for prewarmed instances, we can move to a 6-month pilot.

Attachments: I attached a short metrics extract (FinCrest_Prod_Metrics_Q3.xlsx) and SLO appendix.

Next steps we want from Redwood: an explicit playbook for warm-pool sizing, priming strategy for streaming sessions, and a proposed load-test plan with pass/fail criteria.

Happy to sync this Thursday if you want to run through the playbook.

— Sophie
Head of Product, FinCrest

My read / proposed playbook (initial):

1) Warm pool strategy
- Prewarm 8 instances for the primary region (us-west) for the initial pilot. Reason: customer expects short spikes to 120 concurrency; with our packing and model variant we estimate 8 prewarmed GPUs gives headroom for ~90–110 concurrent streaming sessions depending on model config.
- Priming: use a short priming token sequence to seed KV cache for known prompt templates at session start; this reduces first-response jitter.

2) Scale-up expectations
- Warm pool -> live attach target: 5–12s (fast path) for attach; cold spin-up fallback 40–90s (document). Essential to show warm path in run.

3) Queueing behavior and throttles
- Soft-queue by session (token budget). If concurrency > capacity, prefer token-level thinning and lower-quality model fallback over hard 503.
- Provide visibility: per-request reason codes (queued | throttled | degraded | success) in trace logs.

4) Streaming considerations
- Disable large-batch aggregation for streaming routes; prefer per-session streaming with small batching window (<=10ms) to preserve chunk latency.
- Aim for first-chunk latency <120ms in test (customer asked <100ms; we’ll target <120ms for initial run).

5) Acceptance criteria for Friday run
- p95 first-chunk latency <= 180 ms during 95% of the 30-minute spike window;
- Overall p95 full-response <= 450 ms for 256–512 token responses;
- Warm attach latency median <= 8s; cold spin-up measured and reported separately.

Action items (owners):
- Aditya: produce load test configs (JMeter/locust) for streaming + completions, include both warm-attach and cold-start scenarios.
- Rishi: prepare playbook doc with fallbacks and recommended warm pool counts (deliverable: redwood-proposed-playbook.md).
- Monica: coordinate calendar with FinCrest and confirm Thursday/Friday windows for tests.

Please flag any missing details. If you’re aligned I’ll send Sophie a proposed timeframe and the playbook.

— Camila
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila — I sketched an initial test plan. High level notes:

- Test types: steady-state streaming (60 concurrency), burst ramp (60 -> 120 concurrency over 60s), cold-start exercise (drain then hit new large spike).
- Tools: Locust for stream-socket emulation (we’ll use small chunk intervals), k6 for HTTP-only completion tests. I’ll include a sample Locustfile in the Drive link.
- Model variants: test both q4_0 and q4_1-like quantized builds to see tradeoffs on memory and latency; fallback path: if latency rises >20% at p95, automatically switch non-streaming to smaller variant and continue streaming on primary with degraded chunk size.
- Metrics we’ll collect: first-byte latency, chunk-interval distribution, p50/p95/p99 for full-response, attach latency, GPU utilization, queue length, and reason_code tags.
- Cost estimate: run with 8 prewarmed GPUs + autoscale allowance for 4 extra GPUs for spikes; estimated incremental test cost ~ $1,400 for a 2-hour window.

Schedule proposal:
- Thursday 2027-09-23 16:00–17:30 PT: dry run (internal only)
- Friday 2027-09-24 10:00–11:30 PT: customer-observed run (FinCrest + Redwood)

I linked the preliminary locust and k6 configs on the Drive. Please review and I’ll refine before Thursday dry run.

Attachments: locustfile_streaming_example.py (drive link in related_links)

— Aditya

1) Thursday (internal dry run) — Redwood-only dry run to validate scripts and warm-attach behavior (no customer observers).
2) Friday 10:00 PT — customer-facing load run where we exercise steady state and burst window. Expected duration 75–90 minutes.

Acceptance criteria we’ll confirm live:
- p95 first-chunk latency <= 180 ms during 95% of the spike window (we’ll show distribution charts).
- p95 full-response latency <= 450 ms for 256–512 token requests.
- Warm-attach median <= 8s; cold-start documented and measured.

We’ve attached a short playbook (redwood-proposed-playbook.md) that outlines warm pool sizing, priming sequence, and recommended metrics. Aditya shared the load configs; Monica will send the calendar invite for Friday and a quick 15-min prep touchpoint on Thursday afternoon.
